entries.clue: Marquis's place of origin and deplorable end of life (4)

indicatorNotes.end of: the end of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: a deplorable state of affairs is a sad one
the last letter of LIFE

annotation.surface: A biography note on where a notorious aristocrat came from and how miserably he died.
annotation.walkthrough: The Marquis de Sade's title means 'of Sade': Sade is literally the place he came from, so the definition is exact as well as sly.
annotation.definitionFit: The Marquis de Sade took his title from the family's seat, so Sade is where the marquis came from.

entries.clue: Toadying special address to queen (5)

annotation.definitionNote: Toadying is read as a noun here: 'all that toadying' = 'all that smarm'.

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for special
the Queen is addressed as 'ma'am', also spelt MARM

annotation.surface: A courtier fawning in the special speech he makes to the monarch.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures the toadying itself: a special address to the queen is exactly where you would expect smarm.
annotation.definitionFit: Smarm is oily, ingratiating flattery, which is what toadying is.

entries.clue: Departs on horseback, editor taken for ride (5)

blocks.note: D = departs, as in railway timetables
a jockey who is riding is 'up'
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

annotation.surface: An editor rides off on a horse, apparently taken for a literal ride.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'ride' sound like horse-riding, but 'taken for a ride' is the idiom for being tricked. UP for mounted comes from racing: 'Dettori up'.
annotation.definitionFit: To be taken for a ride is to be cheated or fooled, which is to be duped.

entries.clue: Bloodsucker - run if heard (4)

indicatorNotes.if heard: the word is to be taken by its sound

blocks.note: to run away is to flee, and the spoken word is what counts

annotation.surface: A warning to run for it if you hear a bloodsucker coming.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a vampire warning, which hides the tiny bloodsucker in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: A flea is a parasite that feeds on blood.

entries.clue: German chemist’s whopping whopper comes first (6)

indicatorNotes.comes first: tells you to put the second item, the whopper, before the first

blocks.note: a whopper is a big lie
whopping = very big

annotation.surface: Someone telling an enormous lie at the start of a story about a German scientist.
annotation.walkthrough: Read in order, the clue gives BIG LIE; 'comes first' swaps them. Justus von Liebig was the nineteenth-century chemist behind fertiliser science and the stock cube.
annotation.definitionFit: Justus von Liebig was a leading German chemist of the nineteenth century.

entries.clue: Confused case made for scholastic fields (8)

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A lawyer's muddled argument presented to an academic audience.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Case made' reads like a courtroom phrase, pulling away from the university world of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Academe is the world of scholarship; academes are its separate fields or institutions.

entries.clue: Dead debauchee Donald Duck? (5)

blocks.note: D = dead, as in genealogies
a rake is a dissolute man

annotation.surface: A scandalous suggestion that the cartoon Donald Duck was a dead libertine.
annotation.walkthrough: Donald Duck is a male duck, so he is an example of a drake; the question mark flags that one example standing for the class.
annotation.definitionFit: A drake is a male duck, and Donald is the most famous male duck there is.

entries.clue: He makes spirits from infernal world tense, more evil (9)

blocks.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
T = tense, the grammar abbreviation
ill = evil, so more evil = iller

annotation.surface: A sorcerer summoning spirits from a hellish world that grows tenser and more wicked.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'spirits' ghosts raised from hell; the answer means whisky and gin.
annotation.definitionFit: A distiller makes spirits such as whisky and gin by distillation.

entries.clue: Boy seen in bazaar once (5)

indicatorNotes.seen in: the answer can be seen inside the words that follow

blocks.note: bazAAR ONce

annotation.surface: A boy was once spotted at a market.
annotation.walkthrough: A first name defined as 'Boy' is a standard crossword convention.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Aaron, the biblical brother of Moses, is a common boy's first name.

entries.clue: Stoicism broken under cane thrashing (9)

indicatorNotes.thrashing: a thrashing knocks things about into disorder

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A pupil's stiff upper lip finally giving way while being caned.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue pictures the answer being tested: stoicism is exactly what a caning demands, so the surface and the definition belong together.
annotation.definitionFit: Stoicism is patient endurance of pain or hardship without complaint.

entries.clue: Spaniel regularly seen in boat trip (4)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at a regular interval: here every other one

blocks.note: SpAnIeL: the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters

annotation.surface: A dog that keeps turning up on a boat outing.
annotation.walkthrough: The spaniel on the boat is a pleasant picture that hides a purely letter-level mechanism.
annotation.definitionFit: The noun is named after the canvas that drives the vessel: going for one means an outing on the water.

entries.clue: Pacify primate eating some veg (7)

blocks.note: an ape is a primate
peas are a vegetable

annotation.surface: Calming down a monkey by letting it munch vegetables.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is practical advice: feed the ape to keep it quiet, which is itself appeasement.
annotation.definitionFit: To appease someone is to pacify them by giving them what they want.

entries.clue: Certain ruses deployed in commercial (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the rearranged letters go inside the advertisement

annotation.walkthrough: 'Certain ruses' reads as 'some tricks', but 'Certain' is the definition meaning sure.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an outcome that is guaranteed, with no doubt left, is both certain and sure.

entries.clue: A girl belonging to me hugs a singer (9)

annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this French form of Magdalene is a girl's first name, so 'A girl' stands for it.

entries.clue: For audience get weak beer (3)

annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this top-fermented brew, bitter and pale among them, is one kind of beer.

entries.clue: Victor has tip-off in The Bull Ring (5)

annotation.definitionNote: The inner is strictly the ring just outside the bull on a target; 'in' links it.

indicatorNotes.tip-off: the tip, the first letter, comes off

blocks.note: the victor is the winner; its tip, the W, comes off

annotation.surface: A winner getting a racing tip in the Bull Ring, Birmingham's big shopping centre.
annotation.walkthrough: The Bull Ring is a famous Birmingham shopping district, so the capitals point away from darts and archery, where the inner is the ring round the bull's-eye.
annotation.definitionFit: On a target the inner is the ring immediately around the bull, so it is the bull's ring.

entries.clue: Hip joints need one piano with singer (6)

blocks.note: p = piano, soft in music
Elvis Presley, the singer

annotation.surface: Elvis Presley at the piano, whose swivelling hips were famous.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface earns its keep: Elvis was nicknamed 'Elvis the Pelvis' for his hip movements, so answer and singer are already linked.
annotation.definitionFit: The hip joints are sockets in the pelvis, so each needs one to sit in.

entries.clue: Programming language formats rigged for hardware systems (9)

blocks.note: PL/I is an old programming language; PL is short for programming language
FORMATS rearranged

annotation.surface: A computing note about a language that fixes file formats for hardware.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface stays in computing, so every word looks like part of one technical definition.
annotation.definitionFit: In computing a platform is the hardware and operating system on which software runs.

entries.clue: Delay of time for jailbird (3)

blocks.note: an interval between cause and effect, as with jet travel
British slang for a convict, usually with 'old' in front

annotation.surface: A prisoner's sentence being put back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old lag' is British slang for a long-serving convict, so a lag is a jailbird.
annotation.definitionFit: A lag is an interval of delay, and in slang a convict.

entries.clue: One covers NS&I fraud, standing firm (9)

a sting is a confidence trick

annotation.surface: A whistle-blower firmly exposing a fraud at a government savings bank.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Covers' sounds like a cover-up, but in a down clue it just means 'goes on top of'.

entries.clue: Waterproof clothing waterproofs family (8)

blocks.note: to waterproof a joint is to seal it
one's kin is one's family

annotation.surface: A family kitted out in rain gear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Waterproofs' reads as a plural noun, the family's raincoats; it is a verb meaning seals.
annotation.definitionFit: Sealskin garments are made from seal pelts, naturally water-repellent.

entries.clue: Family cat’s bitten off lamb’s tail (3)

indicatorNotes.bitten off: CAT is bitten off the front of the longer word

blocks.note: a hazel catkin is popularly called a lamb's tail
remove CAT from CATKIN

annotation.surface: A cat biting the tail off a lamb, to the family's horror.
annotation.walkthrough: The farmyard scene hides a botanical fact: the dangling catkins of hazel are called lambs' tails.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: relatives by blood, one's family, are collectively one's kin.

entries.clue: Worked unclean old hotel without a meal (8)

indicatorNotes.Worked: the letters are worked into a new shape
indicatorNotes.without: 'without' means lacking, so the word must go on lacking the letter A

blocks.note: UNCLEAN without its A
O = old
H is Hotel in the phonetic alphabet
the letter taken out of UNCLEAN

annotation.surface: A grubby old hotel that serves no food.
annotation.walkthrough: The complaint about a dirty hotel with no meal hides the meal itself; 'without a' removes one letter A.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: this is the formal word for lunch, the midday meal.

entries.clue: Imperial leader’s gold luxury car touring States (America) (8)

indicatorNotes.touring: the car travels round the States, containing them

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a GT, gran turismo, is a high-performance touring car
the United States
US = America

annotation.walkthrough: 'Imperial leader's' reads as the possessive; the definition is just the leader, Rome's first emperor.

entries.clue: Public relations deceptively nice - Charming? (6)

indicatorNotes.deceptively: NICE is disguised as a different arrangement

blocks.note: PR is public relations
NICE rearranged

entries.clue: Wheel around, turn over (3)

entries.clue: Keeping secret a chastisement (6)

blocks.note: concealing something, putting it out of sight
informal British for a thrashing, as in 'a good ...'

annotation.surface: Concealing a punishment.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'hiding' as a thrashing is informal British English: 'give him a good hiding'.
annotation.definitionFit: Hiding means concealing, and a hiding is a physical punishment.

entries.clue: Stops eating butter etc around sabbath (5)

S = Sabbath, the abbreviation

annotation.walkthrough: The surface is religious abstinence, so 'Stops eating butter' looks like one definition; 'eating' is part of it, and butter is the wordplay.

entries.clue: Don, the cycling Norwegian (5)

entries.clue: Confusion - one of the axes is a stick in the mud (4)

entries.clue: Expel college student not much seen (5)

entries.clue: Program’s second minute up - period of  execution (3,4)

entries.clue: Horses given hitch with head pushed right back (4)

entries.clue: Transported in parcel paper say? (4)
